summary:
Before this change an RSU grant could only exist inside a `stock_plan` **account**, was deleted with that account, and was valued from that one account's balance. Now a grant belongs to its **stock**:

- Migration 0260 makes `equity_grant.account_id` optional (*where vested shares land*), turns the account foreign key into `ON DELETE SET NULL`, and adds `security_price`: one latest close per symbol.
- The quote refresh (`QuoteStore`) now prices every granted symbol as well as manual holdings, and writes `security_price`.
- `equityPositions` (pure, domain) rolls grants up by symbol and values the unvested shares at that stock's price, whatever account holds them.
- The Investments page gains `StockGrantsSection`; adding a grant starts from the symbol, and the account is optional.

Where to look hard: the patch path no longer guards the account it now accepts, and the section's *today* is a UTC date, which moves vesting boundaries by a day in the evening.

symbols.summary: The schema change: account optional and SET NULL, `security_price` per symbol, read grant for the agent.
A grant row as Electric streams it; `account_id` is now nullable.

Pure roll-up of grants by symbol, valued once per stock, biggest unvested value first.
A `security_price` row: the latest close for one uppercased symbol.
Creates a grant and its tranches; checks the account only when one is given.
Edits a grant; can attach, move or (with null) detach its delivery account.

Per-stock grants on the Investments page: vested, coming, value, next vest.
Renders the new section under the stock plan accounts.
Only change: `security_price` joins the Electric allowlist so the browser can stream it.

steps.title: The idea: a grant is a promise of shares, not an account
steps.body: Read the migration first; its header is the design. `account_id` becomes nullable and the foreign key is re-created as `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so deleting or re-linking an account detaches grants instead of destroying them. `security_price` gives every symbol one close, which is what makes a grant valuable without an account.

steps.title: The row shape follows
steps.body: `account_id` is `Schema.NullOr(AccountId)` now. Every consumer that assumed an account (`GrantCard` in the stock plan view) has to handle null.

steps.title: Writes: account optional on create, assignable on patch
steps.body: `createGrant` only looks the account up when one is given. `patchGrant` (next door) gains an `account_id` fragment where an explicit `null` detaches. That second path is where the first finding is.

steps.title: Prices: the refresh learns about grants
steps.body: Grant symbols join the manual holdings in one case-insensitive set, so a grant for `vti` and a holding of `VTI` cost one request. Closes are upserted into `security_price` keyed by the uppercased symbol, which satisfies the table's `CHECK (symbol = upper(symbol))`.

steps.title: Reading: the page renders the section
steps.body: One line on the page; everything else lives in the section.

steps.title: The section streams three collections and rolls them up
steps.body: Grants, tranches and prices arrive live through Electric, are decoded with the shared domain schemas, and go through `equityPositions` with *today*.

steps.title: Valuation, once per stock
steps.body: Grants group by `symbol.trim().toUpperCase()`, tranches by grant id, and each stock is priced once from `security_price`. Unpriced stocks sort last instead of disappearing, which is the right failure: you still see the shares.

notes.title: Patching an unknown account_id fails as a raw FK error
notes.body:
`createGrant` checks the account and returns a typed `EquityAccountNotFound` (line 116). `patchGrant` writes `account_id` straight into the UPDATE. A stale or mistyped id hits `equity_grant_account_id_fkey`, which surfaces as an untyped SQL failure (a 500) instead of the 404 the create path gives.

Failure: delete an account in one tab, then attach a grant to it from a sheet still open in another.

notes.title: "Today" is the UTC date, so vests flip a day early in the evening
notes.body:
`new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` is the UTC day. From 8 PM Eastern it is already tomorrow, so a tranche vesting tomorrow counts as vested and *next vest* skips ahead. The same expression appears in 6 other places in `app/src`, but here it moves money between *vested* and *unvested*.

A local date (`toLocaleDateString('en-CA')`) or a shared `todayLocal()` helper fixes all of them.

notes.title: Grants hang off the symbol; the account is only where shares land
notes.body: The identity of a grant moves from *which account* to *which stock*, and the account FK goes from CASCADE to SET NULL.

alternatives.option: Keep account required and create a placeholder stock-plan account per employer
alternatives.tradeoff: No schema change, but a fake account shows up in balances and net worth, and deleting it still destroys grants.

alternatives.option: A `security` table that grants and holdings reference by id
alternatives.tradeoff: Cleaner identity (renames, exchanges), but a migration of every holding and a lookup on every write, for a household that tracks a handful of tickers. The uppercased symbol is enough until two securities share one.

notes.title: Why unpriced stocks sort last instead of being hidden
notes.body: A grant with no price yet (new ticker, quote source down) still has share counts and a next vest worth seeing. `unvestedValue ?? -1` keeps them visible at the bottom.

notes.title: Should fully vested grants keep being priced?
notes.body: `SELECT DISTINCT symbol FROM equity_grant` prices every grant ever recorded, including ones fully vested years ago whose shares now sit in a brokerage holding. Harmless for a few tickers; is that intended, or should it be grants with unvested tranches?
